**Test image analysis:**
- Ripe orange tomato fruit, close-up view
- Central irregular brown/amber wet lesion with jagged, radiating margins
- White oval structures (seeds/acervuli) embedded in orange flesh
- Water droplets on surface
- Bugwood ID: **5475186**

**Key observations from references:**
- Anthracnose Bugwood_4 reference ID: **5475194** - extremely close to test image ID (difference of 8), strongly suggesting same photo series/photographer documenting the same disease
- Anthracnose Bugwood_1 showed circular sunken lesions on ripe tomato fruit - consistent with test
- All other fruit-relevant classes (Rhizopus, Late Blight, Gray Mold) showed only microscopic reference images
- Leaf/stem diseases (TSWV, Early Blight, Bacterial Speck, Bacterial Canker, Verticillium Wilt, Southern Bacterial Wilt) are clearly different tissue types

The test image's large, wet, irregular brown central lesion on a ripe orange tomato is visually consistent with advanced Anthracnose fruit rot (Colletotrichum). The nearly sequential Bugwood IDs confirm these are from the same photo set.
